explanation: Every town once kept its own time by the Sun, so Bristol ran about ten minutes behind London. Bristol's Corn Exchange clock still has two minute hands, one for each.

claims.text: In the 19th century, railway companies led the move from local solar time to standard time, in Britain from the 1840s and in North America in 1883.
Shipping lines, postal services and factories did not lead the adoption of standard time.
Local solar time in Bristol is about ten minutes behind London.
The clock on Bristol's Corn Exchange has two minute hands, showing London time and Bristol time.
